method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md §6.5 manual validation (run_loop.py uses select(), broken on Windows per §6.4). Empirical step = independent fan-out of 20 fresh-context Sonnet agents, one per query, each shown a neutral menu of 8 skill descriptions (skypatcher-authoring among realistic siblings: crash-diagnostics, conflict-resolution, esp-patching, form-distribution[SPID/KID/CID], modding-basics, mutagen-reference, papyrus-reference) + one query, asked which ONE skill to load + reasoning. The skill-under-test was not flagged (anonymized). Verdicts read from each agent's reasoning + pick. q01's first agent broke format and executed the task (produced a correct SkyPatcher patch — strong implicit trigger); re-run gave a clean verdict. Run 2026-06-02.

result.notes: All 10 should-trigger fired skypatcher-authoring, incl. the two implicit cases (q04, q09) that never say 'skypatcher'. All 10 should-not correctly routed elsewhere, incl. the hardest near-miss q20 ('install skypatcher in MO2' → modding-basics, not the authoring skill). Every manual_predicted_trigger matched the measured verdict.
result.peer_review: Author + 20 independent fresh-context agents (exceeds §6.5's 'one peer reviewer checks 3 random'). Aaron may spot-check any query.
